title: Sep 12 Results + Sep 13 Preview: Twelve Wins and a Whole Lotta Validation
summary: 80% accuracy on Sep 12 slate. Tigers look sharp again for tomorrow's rematch.

content.value:
## Another September Day, Another Solid Performance

You know, I've been around this game long enough to recognize when the model's humming along nicely. Yesterday was one of those days—12 wins out of 15 games will put a smile on anyone's face. At 80% accuracy, we're seeing the kind of consistency that reminds me of those late-season pushes when everything just clicks.

## The Misses Tell a Story Too

Let's get the disappointments out of the way. The Yankees couldn't get it done against the Mets in the Bronx—always a tough cross-town matchup, and those never quite play by the book. The Dodgers falling to the Marlins in Miami? Well, that's baseball in September. Teams resting guys, looking ahead, trap games everywhere. I've seen enough Septembers to know that favorites stumble when you least expect it.

## What Worked Yesterday

The Tigers at 63% confidence? Money. They handled Colorado like we expected. The Rays took care of Houston, the Jays got past Baltimore, and even our coin-flip calls on the Nationals and Twins came through. When your 50-50 picks both hit, you tip your cap to Lady Luck and move on.

The real story is consistency across the board. We had solid reads on pitching matchups, and more importantly, we respected home field in spots where it mattered. That's old-school handicapping meeting modern analytics, and it's a beautiful thing when it works.

## Looking Ahead to Sep 13: Rockies-Tigers, Round Two

Here's where it gets interesting. We're going back to the well with Detroit. The Tigers are facing Colorado again, and our confidence has actually jumped to 69%. Gabriel Hughes takes the ball for the Rockies against Jackson Jobe for Detroit.

I've seen enough Rockies road games to write a book about them—and it wouldn't be a happy read. When you take Colorado out of Coors Field, you're looking at a completely different team. Hughes has shown flashes, but Jobe's been steady at home, and that Tigers lineup has been grinding out quality at-bats all month.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Sep 13
content.sub: 69% win probability • Jackson Jobe (DET) vs Gabriel Hughes (COL)

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

When you hit 80% on a Friday slate, you don't overthink things for Saturday. The Tigers showed us yesterday they're the better team in this matchup. Sometimes the simplest read is the right one—back the home team with the better pitcher against a club that's already thinking about October tee times.

I'll be watching Jobe's command early. If he's locating that fastball like he has been, this one could get out of hand by the sixth inning. Colorado's got nothing to play for, Detroit's still got pride and a home crowd that deserves a winner.

See you tomorrow with the results. Let's make it two straight days above 70%.

author: Max
